proof:
Source: parent proof, step 4 (V7, good points), items (i) and (ii); item (i) is Simon Ch. 1, Theorem 3.26(1), proved via Simon 3.3–3.5 (book/chapter-01.txt), with Simon's normalisation of Hⁿ supplied by the sibling isodiametric_bound (IB): μHE[n] ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)·μH[n].
1. Bounded field. For an n-covector α, |α|² = Σ_{i_1<⋯<i_n}α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n})² ≤ C²‖α‖² with C² the number of increasing multi-indices, since each |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖ (unit vectors). Hence ‖ζ(x)‖ = sup_{‖α‖≤1}|ζ(x)(α)| ≤ sup_{‖α‖≤1}|α| ≤ C for every x.
2. Integrability. ν₀ := Hⁿ⌞M is a finite Borel measure; τ := θζ is strongly measurable and ∫‖τ‖dν₀ ≤ C∫_Mθ dHⁿ < ∞ (θ > 0 on M), so τ ∈ L¹(ν₀; Λ_n).
3. Density comparison (Simon 3.3 for the measure ν₀). Claim: if A₁ ⊆ A₂ ⊆ ℝ^P, τ₀ > 0 and limsup_{ρ↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂ ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) > τ₀ for every x ∈ A₁, then τ₀Hⁿ(A₁) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂). Proof (Simon 3.3–3.5): assume Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) < ∞ (else trivial) and fix δ > 0. The family 𝓑 of closed balls B̄_ρ(x) with x ∈ A₁, 0 < ρ < δ/2 and Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂ ∩ B̄_ρ(x)) ≥ τ₀ω_nρⁿ covers A₁ finely. By the Vitali covering lemma in the form of Simon 3.4(*) (Mathlib Vitali.exists_disjoint_subfamily_covering_enlargement applied to the closed balls with τ := 2) there is a pairwise disjoint subfamily 𝓑' ⊆ 𝓑 such that every B ∈ 𝓑 meets some B' ∈ 𝓑' with radius(B) ≤ 2·radius(B'), hence B ⊆ B̂' (the concentric ball with 5 times the radius). 𝓑' is countable, since its members are disjoint and each has positive measure for the finite measure Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ A₂); enumerate it as B_j = B̄_{ρ_j}(x_j). Then Σ_jω_nρ_jⁿ ≤ τ₀⁻¹Σ_jHⁿ(M ∩ A₂ ∩ B_j) ≤ τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) < ∞. Simon 3.5: for every N, A₁∖⋃_{j≤N}B_j ⊆ ⋃_{j>N}B̄_{5ρ_j}(x_j) — indeed for x ∈ A₁∖⋃_{j≤N}B_j the complement of the closed set ⋃_{j≤N}B_j is a neighbourhood of x, so (fineness) some B ∈ 𝓑 contains x and is disjoint from B_1, …, B_N; the B' ∈ 𝓑' it meets with radius(B) ≤ 2·radius(B') is some B_j with j > N, and x ∈ B ⊆ B̂_j. Thus for every N the sets B_1, …, B_N, B̄_{5ρ_{N+1}}(x_{N+1}), … cover A₁, have diameters ≤ 5δ, and Σ_{j≤N}(2ρ_j)ⁿ + Σ_{j>N}(10ρ_j)ⁿ = (2ⁿ/ω_n)[Σ_{j≤N}ω_nρ_jⁿ + 5ⁿΣ_{j>N}ω_nρ_jⁿ] ≤ (2ⁿ/ω_n)[τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) + 5ⁿΣ_{j>N}ω_nρ_jⁿ]. Hence the 5δ-content inf{Σ_i diam(C_i)ⁿ : A₁ ⊆ ⋃C_i, diam C_i ≤ 5δ} is ≤ inf_N of the right side = (2ⁿ/ω_n)τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂) (the tail of a convergent series tends to 0). Taking the supremum over δ > 0 (the formula of μH[n], Measure.hausdorffMeasure_apply): μH[n](A₁) ≤ (2ⁿ/ω_n)τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂). By (IB) (as measures, setwise also for non-measurable sets, Measure.le_iff'), Hⁿ(A₁) = μHE[n](A₁) ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n](A₁) ≤ τ₀⁻¹Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂).
4. Upper density (i) (Simon 3.26(1)). Let Θ*(x) := limsup_{ρ↓0}Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) and, for t > 1, A_t := {x ∈ M : Θ*(x) > t}. Given ε > 0, outer regularity of the finite Borel measure ν₀ on ℝ^P (Set.exists_isOpen_lt_of_lt; ν₀ is outer regular) gives an open U ⊇ A_t with Hⁿ(M ∩ U) = ν₀(U) ≤ ν₀(A_t) + ε = Hⁿ(A_t) + ε. For x ∈ A_t the small closed balls around x lie in U, so limsup_ρHⁿ(M ∩ U ∩ B̄_ρ(x))/(ω_nρⁿ) = Θ*(x) > t; step 3 with A₁ := A_t, A₂ := U, τ₀ := t gives tHⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ U) ≤ Hⁿ(A_t) + ε. As Hⁿ(A_t) ≤ Hⁿ(M) < ∞ and ε is arbitrary, (t − 1)Hⁿ(A_t) = 0, so Hⁿ(A_t) = 0. Hence {x ∈ M : Θ*(x) > 1} = ⋃_kA_{1+1/k} is Hⁿ-null: (i) holds for Hⁿ-a.e. a ∈ M (with ω_nρⁿ = unitBallVolume n·ofReal(ρⁿ)).
5. Lebesgue points. ℝ^P is finite dimensional, so the Besicovitch Vitali family v := Besicovitch.vitaliFamily ν₀ exists for the finite measure ν₀, and VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_average_norm_sub (or directly the lintegral form VitaliFamily.ae_tendsto_lintegral_enorm_sub_div) gives, for ν₀-a.e. a, ⨍_E‖τ − τ(a)‖dν₀ → 0 along v.filterAt a; by Besicovitch.tendsto_filterAt ν₀ a, r ↦ B̄_r(a) tends to v.filterAt a as r ↓ 0. Hence for ν₀-a.e. a: q(r) := (∫_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖τ − τ(a)‖dHⁿ)/Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) → 0 (for ν₀-a.e. a, a lies in the support of ν₀, so the denominators are positive).
6. (ii). Let a satisfy (i) and step 5. For small r, Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a)) ≤ 2ω_nrⁿ by (i). The lintegral of the integrable function ‖τ − τ(a)‖ over M ∩ B̄_r(a) is ofReal of its integral, so (∫⁻_{M∩B̄_r(a)}‖τ − τ(a)‖dHⁿ)/(ω_nrⁿ) = q(r)·Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 2q(r) → 0 in [0, ∞]. As ‖θ(x)ζ(x) − θ(a)ζ(a)‖ = ‖τ(x) − τ(a)‖, this is (ii).
7. The exceptional sets in steps 4 and 5 are Hⁿ⌞M-null, so (i) and (ii) hold for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. a. ∎
key_steps: ‖ζ‖ is bounded, so τ = θζ ∈ L¹(Hⁿ⌞M).
Simon 3.3 by the 5r-covering lemma, with Hⁿ ≤ (ω_n/2ⁿ)μH[n] from isodiametric_bound, gives τ₀Hⁿ(A₁) ≤ Hⁿ(M ∩ A₂).
Outer regularity and Simon 3.26(1) give limsup Hⁿ(M ∩ B̄_r(a))/(ω_nrⁿ) ≤ 1 a.e.
Besicovitch differentiation with closed balls gives Lebesgue points; combine to get (ii).
